judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the Elementor background-video iframe (YouTube embed, controls=0, role=presentation) behind the hero. Live, the iframe and its .elementor-background-video-container have pointer-events: none, so mouse users cannot operate anything in it either. It has no controls and offers no function, so 2.1.1 has nothing to require keyboard access for. The rule treated a decorative frame as a 'native control'. judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the 'O Museu' submenu container (div role=button, tabindex 0) in the main nav at 369,87 in a 1280x800 window. The welcome modal (#premium-modal-cbfd80b, 'Bem vindo ao museu') opens by itself a few seconds after load, does not take or contain focus (activeElement stays on body, Tab goes to the page behind it, Escape only works with focus inside it), and its white dialog box is opaque (rgb(255,255,255), 700x650 at x 290-990, y 75-725 in a 1280x800 window; 390x694 at y 75-769 in a 390x844 window) over a semi-transparent rgba(0,0,0,.5) backdrop. Live in headless Edge with the modal open, focusing this element changed 0 px in its area because it sits entirely under the opaque dialog box; with the modal closed the same element shows a black outline focus indicator (it is not missing in the CSS). So the cause is obscuring, not missing styling, but the finding names that cause, and the 2.4.11 Understanding says a fully obscured focus indicator would likely fail 2.4.7 as well; in the state a keyboard user meets on load no indicator is visible.

The welcome modal (#premium-modal-cbfd80b, 'Bem vindo ao museu') opens by itself a few seconds after load, does not take or contain focus (activeElement stays on body, Tab goes to the page behind it, Escape only works with focus inside it), and its white dialog box is opaque (rgb(255,255,255), 700x650 at x 290-990, y 75-725 in a 1280x800 window; 390x694 at y 75-769 in a 390x844 window) over a semi-transparent rgba(0,0,0,.5) backdrop. The modal is not opened by the user, so Note 2 does not apply, and the Understanding names an overlay that lets focus exit into the content behind it as the failing case. Checked live: with the modal open the element's centre hit-tests to the dialog and its focus ring does not show. The focused component is entirely hidden by author content: 2.4.11 fails.
